subject: PII audit proofpoints + on-prem connectivity paths
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: PI I audit proofpoints + on-prem connectivity paths

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and actions from our discovery on private deployment and data handling. High level: MedLytics wants an on-prem/private deployment with strict PII residency (US-only), 90-day retention for raw logs, and full request/response audit logs accessible for a 12-month window for compliance reviews. They also asked about running inference in an air-gapped mode and what telemetry (if any) leaves the customer's VPC.

Action items (owner in parentheses):
- Confirm whether Redwood can run in a fully air-gapped mode with zero outbound egress (Logan)
- Provide a concise SOC2 + data-flow proofpoint document referencing what logs are generated and stored (Neha)
- Share a minimal network diagram template showing agent/edge->onprem runtime flows and where, if anywhere, metadata might transit (Marissa)
- Get MedLytics procurement contact and ask for standard NDA + expected procurement timeline (Aisha/Tom)

Attachments: call recording stub, draft questionnaire (referenced below).

Notes from call:
- MedLytics will not allow any PII to be stored outside their air-gapped environment; they want a defined retention policy for different classes: raw request traces (90 days), aggregated metrics (indefinite but not PII), and KV cache (customer-controlled deletion).
- They want a toggle to disable all async telemetry by default; acceptable mechanims for debug-only telemetry under signed-off incident processes.

Please review and I'll follow up with Neha's security summary and a network drawing.

— Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medlytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <t.ruiz@medlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: PI I audit proofpoints + on-prem connectivity paths

Thanks Logan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side before procurement: 
- Air-gapped requirement: we need the option to run inference on a closed network for certain workloads. If you can provide a documented process for initial model load (how models are transferred into the environment) and periodic updates (signed packages, checksum verification), that would cover most concerns.
- Logging: we want a clear classification table mapping what is considered PII vs. non-PII, and a mechanism to automatically redact or pseudonymize before any persistent storage. Is Redwood able to expose an API toggle (per-deployment) for pseudonymization?
- Audit access: 3rd-party auditors may request logs for a rolling 12 months; we need guidance on export formats and time-to-export SLA.

Tom and procurement will want to see any certs / attestation for the deployment mode and a short runbook for incident response that we can attach to our contract.

We'll attach a sample data map and preferred NDA templates later today.

— Aisha
Head of Ops, MedLytics
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medlytics.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PI I audit proofpoints + on-prem connectivity paths

Hi Aisha — quick security-first responses inline below.

On air-gapped deploys and model transfer:
- We support an air-gapped deployment pattern: initial model/artifact import is done via signed tarball over an operator-controlled media transfer (S3 export -> offline transfer) or via a secure USB using our import verifier. We provide SHA256 checksums and a signing key that your ops team can verify. No outbound telemetry is sent by default.

On logging and redaction/pseudonymization:
- Redwood can enable per-deployment pseudonymization that hashes or tokenizes user identifiers before storage; that feature is configurable and can be enforced via deployment policy. We will provide a config snippet and a reference implementation for common languages.
- Classification mapping: attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) you'll find our PII mapping table and which logs contain what fields. For anything marked as PII we can configure either immediate redaction or retention-limited storage.

On auditor exports and SLA:
- We can export audit logs in newline-delimited JSON or Parquet (your choice). Typical export prep time for <30GB is <4 hours; larger exports have a runbook. We'll include an export SLA in the runbook.

On incident response runbook:
- Draft runbook will be included in the private-deploy packet; it covers on-call contacts, evidence collection (hash lists, S3 manifests), and approved remote access steps if you permit. For strictly air-gapped installs we rely on operator-provided physical media for deep forensics.

Attaching: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (contains mapping and cert references) and a starter network sketch (private-deploy-network-drawings.png).

Let me know if you want a brief 30-minute security walkthrough with our engineering ops team this week.

— Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Aisha / Tom — thanks for the quick reply. Next steps from sales ops side: 
- I'll send a short checklist (one-pager) that MedLytics can use to confirm network readiness and firewall rules; it includes expected ports, package checksum verification steps, and a list of optional telemetry flags.
- Can you confirm the preferred names/emails for procurement? We'll push an initial SOW + NDA and a DocuSign link for the standard private deployment addendum.

Proposed timeline: security walkthrough with Neha this week, network readiness checklist returned by MedLytics within 3 business days, and procurement stage opened next week pending NDA.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/medlytics-sla-8421 (stub — will send formal envelope).
